title: Preferred Employer Rate — Renewal History Step (Apartment Home Lease)
content:
**Rate memorandum — preferred employer program, Apartment Home Lease.**

The preferred employer rate of an Apartment Home Lease is raised by a renewal step for the renewal rent changes recorded on the lease's Lease Term Agreements: three or more renewal rent changes on record raise it by 0.010, one or two raise it by 0.005, and none leaves it unchanged.

## Step schedule

| Renewal rent changes recorded on the lease's Lease Term Agreements | Renewal step added to the preferred employer rate |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | 0.010 (one percentage point, 1%) |
| 1 or 2 | 0.005 (half a percentage point, 0.5%) |
| 0 | nothing |

**Records read.** The rent change records of the Lease Term Agreement charter for the customer's lease, counting those whose reason is a renewal. Rent changes for any other reason — a month-to-month conversion or a transfer — are not renewal rent changes and are not counted.

**Effect.** The step raises the preferred employer rate itself; the raised rate is the rate applied to the period's base rent line.

## Boundaries

- 2 renewal rent changes: step 0.005. A third renewal rent change moves the lease to 0.010.
- 0 renewal rent changes: no step. A first renewal rent change moves the lease to 0.005.

## Example (hypothetical)

A lease on a floor plan rate of 0.05 with 4 renewal rent changes on its Lease Term Agreements carries a preferred employer rate raised to 0.06; with 1 renewal rent change, to 0.055. The floor plan rate and the counts are example inputs.
